{
  "success_memory_items": [
    {
      "title": "Write a temporary self-test harness before trusting the implementation",
      "pattern": "After implementing the target module, immediately create a throwaway test script (e.g. selftest.mjs / tmp_selftest.mjs) that imports the real module and asserts expected outputs, then run it with node. Keep the harness separate from the deliverable and delete it before finishing.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden grader cannot be inspected, so a local harness is the only feedback loop. It converts the spec into executable checks, surfaces wrong assumptions early, and lets the agent iterate on the real module rather than guessing.",
      "examples": [
        "Wrote selftest.mjs importing { encode, decode } and asserting known ciphertexts, then ran `node selftest.mjs`.",
        "Wrote tmp_selftest.mjs for robot-name asserting name format, uniqueness across 300+ robots, and reset behavior.",
        "Wrote selfcheck.mjs for zebra-puzzle asserting waterDrinker()/zebraOwner() and that exactly one arrangement satisfies all facts."
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises where the official test file is hidden.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Build an independent reference model for differential testing",
      "pattern": "For algorithmic tasks, implement a second, deliberately different computation of the expected result (brute-force search, exhaustive enumeration, or a naive direct formula) and compare it against the real implementation over many generated inputs.",
      "why_it_helps": "A second independent model catches errors that a hand-written example set misses, especially in modular arithmetic, tie-breaking, and combinatorial edge cases. Agreement across hundreds of cases is much stronger evidence than a few fixed examples.",
      "examples": [
        "gen.mjs brute-forced the modular inverse over a in 1..25 and compared against the real encode/decode for many keys.",
        "verify2.tmp.mjs enumerated all reachable tic-tac-toe boards by legal play and compared states against gamestate().",
        "killer-sudoku selftest included 'brute-force agreement (460 cases)' against a naive combination generator.",
        "ledger differential test compared the refactor against a saved copy of the original implementation over 1232 cases."
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks with a well-defined mathematical or combinatorial specification.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Treat the spec text as the source of truth for exact output strings",
      "pattern": "When the spec contains literal expected output (lyrics, tables, formatted numbers), encode those exact strings in the self-test and compare character-for-character, including punctuation, capitalization, and blank lines.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders often compare exact strings. Subtle differences like a missing period, wrong capitalization, or an extra blank line cause failures that logic-only tests would miss.",
      "examples": [
        "bottle-song test embedded the full expected song text and caught 'There'll be Nine' vs 'nine' capitalization.",
        "house test caught missing trailing period in 'This is the house that Jack built.'",
        "tournament test asserted the exact header line and its length (55 chars)."
      ],
      "scope": "Exercises whose output is prose, formatted tables, or fixed text.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Probe boundary and degenerate inputs explicitly",
      "pattern": "Enumerate and test the boundary cases the spec implies: zero/empty inputs, minimum and maximum sizes, invalid keys, non-coprime values, out-of-range numbers, and inputs that should throw.",
      "why_it_helps": "Most hidden-test failures come from boundaries rather than the happy path. Explicit boundary tests force the implementation to handle them and reveal off-by-one or missing-validation bugs.",
      "examples": [
        "affine-cipher tested a=0 and non-coprime a to confirm an error is thrown.",
        "triangle tested degenerate sides (1,1,2) and zero-length sides.",
        "phone-number tested exchange codes starting with 0 or 1 and area codes starting with 0 or 1.",
        "space-age tested exact multiples of an Earth year and the 1e9-second example."
      ],
      "scope": "All exercises with validation rules or numeric ranges.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Verify the module's public interface and syntax before finishing",
      "pattern": "Run `node --check <file>` for syntax and a small import that prints the exported names and a sample call, confirming the module exports exactly what the grader expects.",
      "why_it_helps": "A syntax error or a wrong export name fails every test regardless of logic. A cheap final check catches these before submission.",
      "examples": [
        "`node --check affine-cipher.js && node -e \"import('./affine-cipher.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m)))\"` confirmed exports decode,encode.",
        "`node --check triangle.js` before running the self-test.",
        "`node --check zebra-puzzle.js && echo SYNTAX OK`."
      ],
      "scope": "All single-file JS exercises.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up temporary artifacts and confirm the final directory state",
      "pattern": "After tests pass, delete all temporary test/reference files and list the directory to confirm only the deliverable and original scaffolding remain.",
      "why_it_helps": "Leftover helper files can confuse the grader or violate the instruction not to create test files. A final listing verifies the workspace is clean.",
      "examples": [
        "`rm -f selftest.mjs && ls -a` after affine-cipher.",
        "`rm -f temp_diag.mjs temp_selftest.mjs && node --check bottle-song.js && ls -A`.",
        "`rm -f _orig_reference.mjs _selftest.mjs _selftest2.mjs _selftest3.mjs && node --check ledger.js && ls -a`."
      ],
      "scope": "All exercises where temporary files were created.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Isolate the failing case with a minimal diagnostic script",
      "pattern": "When a test fails, write a tiny script that prints the actual value, its type, and character codes for the specific failing input, rather than re-reading the whole implementation.",
      "why_it_helps": "Direct inspection of the actual output (including invisible characters like non-breaking spaces or line endings) pinpoints the bug faster than reasoning about the code.",
      "examples": [
        "Printed character codes of the ledger change column to discover a non-breaking space (U+00A0).",
        "Printed JSON of each character in a tic-tac-toe board to find a wrong diagonal test fixture.",
        "Printed line lengths of OCR input rows to confirm the 3-column grid width."
      ],
      "scope": "Debugging exact-output or formatting mismatches.",
      "confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "title": "Preserve the original implementation as a differential oracle when refactoring",
      "pattern": "For refactoring exercises, save a copy of the original working code and compare the refactored output against it across many inputs before deleting the copy.",
      "why_it_helps": "The original code is known to pass the tests, so it is a reliable oracle. Differential testing guarantees the refactor preserves behavior, which is the whole point of the exercise.",
      "examples": [
        "ledger: saved _orig_reference.mjs and ran 1232 differential cases with zero diffs.",
        "ledger: compared sorted rows and change-column formatting between old and new implementations."
      ],
      "scope": "Refactoring exercises where a working baseline exists.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    }
  ]
}
